question: What is the primary reason for removing surgical sutures on schedule?

options.A: To immediately eliminate the need for any further dressings
options.B: To prevent the skin from developing a darker pigmentation
options.C: To accelerate the complete closure of deeper muscle layers
options.D: To prevent permanent skin marking from suture tracks

explanation: Leaving sutures in too long causes the epithelial tissue to grow around the thread, leading to permanent track marks and difficult removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Leaving surgical sutures in place past the expected healing time can lead to which clinical issue?

options.A: Rapid softening of the surrounding dermal layer
options.B: Increased foreign body reaction and scarring
options.C: Immediate liquefactive necrosis of the wound margins
options.D: Spontaneous re-opening of the deep tissue layers

explanation: The body treats prolonged suture material as a foreign object, provoking unnecessary inflammation and worse scarring. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Facial sutures are typically removed much sooner than sutures on the leg because of...

options.A: the constant application of facial cosmetics
options.B: higher blood supply and rapid healing
options.C: less exposure to dust and environmental dirt
options.D: thinner skin that tears easily under pressure

explanation: The face has an abundant vascular network which speeds up tissue repair and necessitates early removal to prevent scarring. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: A patient with a laceration over the knee joint asks why their stitches stay in for two weeks. What is your best response?

options.A: Leg skin is much thicker than other parts of the body and grows slower.
options.B: Knee wounds always get infected if stitches are removed before fourteen days.
options.C: Joints experience high movement and tension, requiring more time to heal safely.
options.D: The doctor forgot to schedule the removal earlier in the week.

explanation: High-tension areas like joints need extended support to prevent the healing wound from pulling apart with movement. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: What should the nurse do first when noticing partial separation of the wound edges during pre-assessment?

options.A: Apply a strong antiseptic and proceed carefully
options.B: Cover the area with dry gauze and send the patient home
options.C: Stop the removal and report to the physician
options.D: Remove every alternate stitch to relieve tension

explanation: Partial wound separation indicates inadequate healing, and pulling remaining sutures will cause total wound breakdown. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: Which finding represents a clear contraindication to proceeding with suture removal?

options.A: Dry scabbing over the small puncture tracks
options.B: Purulent discharge along the incision line
options.C: Mild itching reported around the healing scar
options.D: Slight pinkness directly adjacent to the knot

explanation: Pus indicates active infection, meaning the wound is unstable and may require retention sutures or drainage. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: Which instrument feature makes a suture scissor specifically safe for cutting skin stitches?

options.A: A serrated blade designed to grip thick nylon cord
options.B: A curved blunt edge to prevent accidental skin pinching
options.C: A small hooked tip to slide easily under the thread
options.D: An extra-long handle for deep surgical cavity access

explanation: The tiny hook on stitch scissors slips under the exposed suture loop without catching or injuring the delicate skin underneath. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why is normal saline or antiseptic used to clean the suture line before cutting the threads?

options.A: To numb the superficial nerve endings in the skin
options.B: To soften dried crusts and remove surface bacteria
options.C: To dissolve the nylon material before pulling it out
options.D: To permanently seal the tiny puncture holes instantly

explanation: Cleaning clears away dried exudate and surface pathogens, ensuring they do not get pulled down into the tissue tracts during removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the correct method for dealing with a running or continuous suture during removal?

options.A: Soak the continuous line in warm water until the thread dissolves
options.B: Grab the main knot and yank the entire thread out in one fast pull
options.C: Cut every single knot individually and leave the loops inside the skin
options.D: Snip each loop and pull the strand out carefully from one end

explanation: Cutting each loop prevents dragging contaminated exterior suture material through the internal skin tracks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What complication can occur if a tiny fragment of suture material is accidentally left inside the skin?

options.A: Rapid absorption of the fragment into the bloodstream
options.B: Immediate breakdown of the entire subcutaneous layer
options.C: Permanent discoloration of the surrounding epidermis
options.D: Delayed foreign body reaction and granuloma formation

explanation: Any leftover foreign body acts as an irritant, often causing a localized inflammatory nodule or granuloma weeks later. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why are adhesive closure strips often placed across a wound immediately after suture removal?

options.A: To provide extra mechanical support to the vulnerable new scar
options.B: To stop any deep arterial bleeding from the incision site
options.C: To completely replace the skin's natural protective lipid layer
options.D: To hide any remaining redness from the patient's sight

explanation: Adhesive strips help bear minor mechanical loads during the early remodeling phase when tensile strength is still building up. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the immediate nursing action if a wound begins to gape open while you are cutting out stitches?

options.A: Finish cutting all remaining stitches quickly to apply dressing
options.B: Apply heavy pressure with gauze until the bleeding stops
options.C: Wash the open area immediately with strong hydrogen peroxide
options.D: Stop removing the remaining stitches and secure the edges

explanation: Stopping prevents further wound disruption, and securing the remaining stitches protects the open area until the doctor evaluates it. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard documentation requirement following suture removal?

options.A: The overall physical condition and appearance of the incision
options.B: The exact brand and manufacturer name of the original thread
options.C: The total number of sutures successfully removed from the site
options.D: Any patient education given regarding post-removal care

explanation: Brand names of removed sutures are unnecessary for the clinical record; total count, wound condition, and care instructions are what matter. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)
